casual_social.description: Default Indian B2C — Hinglish-heavy, expressive, warm.

professional_casual.description: LinkedIn India — light Hinglish, mostly English.

corporate_formal.description: Standard British-leaning Indian English for business.

grammar_quirks: Habitual present where US would use simple present ('I am eating' for routine eating)
Reduplication for emphasis (very very good, hot hot)

code_switching_patterns.english_in_hindi: Hinglish — heavy mixing, especially in urban Tier-1 cities (Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore). Sentences flip between Hindi and English mid-clause naturally.
rules: Hinglish is regionally variable — Mumbai Hinglish ≠ Delhi Hinglish
South India (Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam states) uses less Hindi mixing — adapt to Tamil/Telugu English where relevant
B2B India often defaults to mostly-English with light yaar/bhai inserts

do_not_use: Stereotyped Indian English ('please do the needful immediately' as parody)

example_translations.note: Hinglish flow: English structure with Hindi anchor word.
